content:
Monday’s announcement that Robert Pattinson would be the next 007 understandably drew plenty of attention — including from the royal family.

He also got support from a man who probably knows what Pattinson will face as he takes on the role of one of cinema’s most beloved characters.

Former James Bond star George Lazenby, who played the superspy in only one film, 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service,” in a social media post welcomed Pattinson “to the most exclusive club in the world.”

In a brief message, the 87-year-old Australian actor also offered some advice to his 40-year-old counterpart: “Remember to enjoy yourself.”

Lazenby also cheekily told Pattinson, “Let’s see if you’ll have ‘This never happened to the other fella’ moment,” before wishing him, “All the best, mate.”

Lazenby’s “other fella” refers to an early scene in “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service” where Bond is left alone on a beach after rescuing Diana Rigg from a group of thugs, leading his character to break the fourth wall and comment to the audience.

None of the other surviving Bond actors ― Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan or Timothy Dalton ― had commented on Pattinson’s casting as of Tuesday afternoon.
